answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent audits catch fabricated work. Auditors sample claims and compare them with task outputs; a false claim risks losing the deposit, while honest agents recover it after a challenge window. This makes spawning sybils costly: an attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks forfeiting it, rather than gaining influence by minting names as cheaply as pigment on a reef beside a jetty.
